answer: Silo stores a checkpoint outside the computer, on the machine that runs it, on the same drive as the computer's own disk, since a copy that shares blocks can live only there. Nothing inside any computer can reach it, and it never changes once saved. A checkpoint is removed whole or not at all: by thinning, when its computer leaves the bin for good, or by you.

sets.says: A checkpoint never changes, and nothing inside a computer can reach it.
